summary_paragraph: The patient with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by post-bypass hypoglycemia requiring tube feeds, multiple gastrostomy placements, and subsequent bypass reversal was admitted to the surgery service for two days of epigastric/mid-abdominal burning pain with nausea and inability to tolerate solid oral intake, with one red-tinged brown emesis on arrival. Evaluation included labs without acute abnormalities and an upper GI contrast study showing no leak, stricture, or obstruction (mild reflux noted). Nutrition was managed via G-tube with careful formula and rate adjustments after intolerance to Vivonex at higher rates; she ultimately tolerated Jevity 1.5 at goal 45 mL/hr with manageable baseline nausea after antiemetic adjustment to prochlorperazine as needed and addition of erythromycin for motility. Given her hypoglycemia history, she was monitored closely and supported with dextrose-containing IV fluids until stable on goal tube feeds with stable blood sugars and hemodynamics, then discharged home ambulatory with tube-feeding instructions, medication updates, and surgical clinic follow-up.
problems: Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without hemorrhage or perforation
